_meta.description: CO2 (and now CH4/N2O) emission factors for fuel combustion and grid electricity.
_meta.critical_caveat: CPCB does NOT publish CO2/GHG emission factors -- its mandate is criteria pollutants (PM, SOx, NOx, CO) and compliance, not carbon accounting. IPCC is the source for fuel-combustion CO2/CH4/N2O factors used here. GRID ELECTRICITY emission factor -- previously the single biggest gap in this file -- has now been filled directly from CEA's primary published database (see grid_electricity below).
_meta.last_verified: 2026-08-16 -- grid electricity factor fetched directly from CEA CO2 Baseline Database User Guide Version 21.0 (published November 2025, PDF); CH4/N2O Tier 1 factors fetched directly from the IPCC 2006 Guidelines Vol.2 Ch.2 primary PDF, Table 2.3 (Manufacturing Industries and Construction category, the correct one for MSME factory combustion)

fuel_combustion_tier1_ipcc.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National GHG Inventories, Vol.2 Ch.2 (Stationary Combustion), Table 2.3 (Manufacturing Industries and Construction) for CH4/N2O, and Table 1.4 for CO2 -- global Tier 1 defaults, fetched directly from the primary PDF this pass

biomass_wood.note: IPCC 'Wood/Wood Waste' row, Table 2.3. is_biogenic=true for the CO2 component (see biogenic_co2_treatment); CH4/N2O are NOT excluded from totals even for biomass.

peat.note: Table 2.3 'Peat' row. Not a typical MSME fuel in India -- included only for completeness of the original compile.

coking_coal.note: Table 2.3 'Coking Coal' row. 'Other Bituminous Coal' (best proxy for most Indian non-coking industrial coal) has an identical CH4/N2O factor (10 / 1.5 kg/TJ) even though its CO2 factor differs slightly (94,600 for coking vs 94,600-99,700 range for other bituminous) -- see india_specific_coal_caveat below.

lpg.note: Table 2.3 'Liquefied Petroleum Gases' row -- added this pass since energy_prices.json now has commercial LPG pricing but this file previously had no LPG emission factor at all.

converted_practical_units.conversion_method: kg CO2/tonne fuel = NCV x CO2_EF / 1000, then converted to per-kg/per-litre/per-Nm3 using standard reference densities (diesel 0.832 kg/L, petrol 0.74 kg/L, natural gas 0.717 kg/Nm3)
converted_practical_units.conversion_status: Derived by the researcher, not directly IPCC-published -- good enough as a model default, should be cross-checked (e.g. against India GHG Program fuel factor sheet) before treating as citation-grade. NOT re-derived for CH4/N2O this pass -- the kg/TJ figures above are the primary-sourced values; per-litre/per-kg CH4/N2O conversions would need the same density-based derivation applied to CO2 below, not yet done.

biomass_wood.accounting_note: Excluded from net totals under IPCC methodology (see biogenic_co2_treatment below) -- treat as ~0 net CO2 for decarbonization-benefit calculations. CH4/N2O from biomass combustion are NOT excluded -- see ch4_n2o_factors below, now filled with real values (30 kg CH4/TJ, 4 kg N2O/TJ), notably higher than fossil fuels' CH4/N2O factors.

fuel_combustion_tier1_ipcc.india_specific_coal_caveat: Indian industrial coal does not map cleanly to 'Anthracite' or 'Lignite' -- most MSME boiler coal is a lower/mid-grade blend. The two coal rows above should be treated as bracketing bounds, not a precise match, unless a BEE/CEA India-specific figure is available. NOTE: the CEA CO2 Baseline Database (see grid_electricity below) DOES contain an India-specific, measured coal emission factor for power-sector coal -- 0.969 tCO2/MWh net generation for coal-fired stations (FY2024-25) -- but this is expressed per unit of ELECTRICITY OUTPUT (i.e. already reflects the plant's heat rate/efficiency), not per unit of fuel INPUT, so it is not directly substitutable for the IPCC per-tonne-of-coal figures above without a heat-rate conversion. Still no direct India-specific INR-fuel-input-basis coal CO2 factor for industrial boiler use.

biogenic_co2_treatment.rule: Per IPCC methodology, CO2 from biomass combustion is reported as a memo item, not counted in national/sectoral totals -- it is assumed to be part of the natural carbon cycle (recaptured by regrowth). Counting it as a straight emission would double-count against the AFOLU (land use) sector.
biogenic_co2_treatment.modeling_implication: When a lever recommends switching coal to biomass, the CO2 benefit is larger than a naive fuel-swap calculation suggests, because the biomass leg approaches near-zero net CO2 in standard accounting (CH4/N2O still count, CO2 largely does not). This should be encoded as an is_biogenic boolean flag per fuel, not silently applied. Now that real biomass CH4 (30 kg/TJ) and N2O (4 kg/TJ) factors are available -- both notably higher than fossil fuel factors -- the CH4/N2O side of a coal-to-biomass switch is not negligible and should be included in the model, not treated as a rounding error.

grid_electricity.status: FILLED -- fetched directly from the primary CEA source this pass
grid_electricity.source: Central Electricity Authority, 'CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector', User Guide Version 21.0, published November 2025, covering FY 2024-25 data. Fetched directly from the CEA-hosted PDF (cea.nic.in).
grid_electricity.which_variant_to_use: For a straightforward 'how much CO2 does this MSME's grid electricity use represent' calculation -- the kind this whole model needs -- use the WEIGHTED AVERAGE (0.71 tCO2/MWh). This is confirmed by the CEA guide's own worked example (Section 6.2): 'An industry consuming 100 MUs of power from the grid... Total CO2 Emissions = 70,000 MWh x 0.710 tCO2/MWh'. The other three variants (OM, BM, CM) are for CDM/carbon-credit project accounting (calculating emissions AVOIDED by a new renewable energy project displacing grid power) -- not the right variant for a straightforward consumption-based footprint calculation. Do not substitute OM/BM/CM for a simple consumption emissions figure.
grid_electricity.worked_example_formula: Total CO2 Emissions (tCO2) = Grid electricity consumed (MWh) x 0.710. E.g. 100,000 kWh/year consumption = 100 MWh x 0.710 = 71 tCO2/year.
grid_electricity.trend_note: Grid factor has declined from 0.774 (FY2013-14) to 0.710 (FY2024-25), reflecting rising renewable generation share -- useful if the model projects future-year emissions savings and wants a declining-grid-factor assumption rather than a flat one. FY2023-24 (0.727) was a local peak/anomaly year.

fossil_fuel_specific_factors_tco2_per_mw.note: These are per unit of ELECTRICITY OUTPUT from that fuel type's power stations (already reflect real Indian plant heat rates/efficiency), not per unit of fuel input -- useful if the model needs to distinguish 'displacing coal power' vs 'displacing gas power' scenarios, e.g. for open-access/green-tariff modeling, but not a substitute for the IPCC per-tonne fuel-input factors used elsewhere in this file.

grid_electricity.green_tariff_open_access_note: Per the CEA guide's own example: electricity procured through green open access or a green tariff mechanism 'may be considered as zero' emission factor -- relevant if the model ever needs to handle an MSME that has signed a renewable PPA or green tariff rather than drawing standard grid power.
grid_electricity.version_currency_note: CEA updates this database annually. Version 21.0 (Nov 2025, FY2024-25 data) is current as of this pass (Aug 2026). Check cea.nic.in for a newer version (V22.0, expected ~Nov 2026) if this file is used after that point -- the trend above shows the factor moves by roughly 0.01-0.02 tCO2/MWh per year, so a one-year-stale figure is a small but non-zero error.

ch4_n2o_factors.status: FILLED -- fetched directly from the primary IPCC PDF this pass (Table 2.3, Manufacturing Industries and Construction category -- the correct category for MSME factory combustion, as opposed to Table 2.2 Energy Industries/power generation or Table 2.4/2.5 commercial/residential)
ch4_n2o_factors.note: Values below are duplicated for convenience from fuel_combustion_tier1_ipcc.raw_energy_basis_factors above -- same source, same table.
ch4_n2o_factors.gwp_note: To convert to CO2e, apply Global Warming Potential (GWP) multipliers: CH4 and N2O factors above are NOT yet GWP-weighted. Common values: CH4 GWP-100 = 28-30 (AR5/AR6), N2O GWP-100 = 265-273 (AR5/AR6) -- exact multiplier depends which IPCC Assessment Report the model wants to align with. This file does not currently specify which AR the model should use -- flagging as a decision the model owner needs to make, not a research gap.
ch4_n2o_factors.biomass_significance_note: Biomass CH4 (30 kg/TJ) and N2O (4 kg/TJ) factors are 3-10x higher than fossil fuel factors for the same gases. Since biomass CO2 is excluded from net accounting but CH4/N2O are not, a coal-to-biomass switch's true net CO2e benefit is smaller than a 'CO2 only' calculation would suggest -- this is exactly the modeling risk flagged in biogenic_co2_treatment above, and it is now quantifiable rather than just a qualitative warning.

cpcb_note.role: Compliance/regulatory only -- criteria pollutants (PM, SOx, NOx, CO), not GHG accounting. See industry_defaults.json for CPCB's boiler PM limits and Red/Orange/Green/White/Blue categorization, which are compliance-cost inputs, not emission-factor inputs.

gaps_and_flags: GRID ELECTRICITY emission factor: RESOLVED this pass. 0.710 tCO2/MWh (weighted average, FY2024-25, CEA Version 21.0) is the figure to use for standard consumption-based footprint calculations -- fetched directly from the primary CEA PDF, including the CEA's own worked example confirming this is the right variant to use.

CH4 and N2O Tier 1 factors: RESOLVED this pass. Fetched directly from the primary IPCC PDF, Table 2.3 (Manufacturing Industries and Construction -- the correct category). Not yet GWP-weighted into CO2e -- see gwp_note above, which flags this as a modeling decision (which IPCC Assessment Report's GWP values to use) rather than a data gap.
LPG emission factor: RESOLVED this pass (was entirely absent before) -- CO2 63,100 kg/TJ, CH4 1 kg/TJ, N2O 0.1 kg/TJ, matching the LPG pricing now available in energy_prices.json.

Tier 2 (India-specific) coal factors on a FUEL-INPUT basis are still missing -- Tier 1 global defaults (Anthracite/Lignite) remain the bracketing proxies for Indian industrial boiler coal. Note: CEA's database DOES have an India-specific coal factor, but it's expressed per unit of electricity OUTPUT (0.969 tCO2/MWh, already reflecting power-plant heat rate), not per unit of coal INPUT -- not directly usable for an industrial boiler calculation without a heat-rate conversion. This remains a genuine, narrower gap.

Litre/Nm3 unit conversions for CO2 are researcher-derived, not IPCC-published directly -- worth a second-source cross-check before being cited as authoritative. The equivalent litre/Nm3 conversions for the newly-added CH4/N2O factors have NOT been derived this pass -- only the kg/TJ figures are filled; a follow-up pass would need to apply the same density-based conversion method used for CO2.

Grid electricity factor will need an annual refresh -- CEA typically publishes a new version each November/December. This file's 0.710 tCO2/MWh figure is current for FY2024-25 (Version 21.0, Nov 2025) as of this update; check for Version 22.0 if used after ~November 2026.
